AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called meeting to order at 5:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL Councilmember Rebollo arrived at 5:12 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:15 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items:

Item #2.C and #4.C  - Staff provided presentation, direction was provided and no reportable action was taken on these items.  

City Council convened to Closed Session after the regular City Council meeting and reconvened at 9:20 p.m.

Item #1 - Staff provided presentation, City Council provided feedback and no reportable action was taken on this item.  

Items #4.B and #4.C - staff made a presentation, direction was provided by the City Council and no reportable action was taken on this item.  

Items #2.A, #2.B, #3, and #4.A were not discussed in the Closed Session. 


6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:16 p.m.

ROLL CALL

INVOCATION Councilmember Garcia offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

10.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte presented statistical data for the preceding two weeks. During this period, deputies engaged in various activities, including attending social media training and showing their support for LASD breast cancer awareness by donning pink patches. They also participated in Red Ribbon Week by wearing red patches.

1.. Proclamation Declaring October 23-31, 2022 as “Red Ribbon Week” in the City of Commerce Assistant City Manager Domic introduced the new Public Safety Manager, Justin Edson.

Mr. Edson expressed his enthusiasm for working with the team and proceeded to give an overview of the significance of Red Ribbon Week.

Mayor Argumedo then read the proclamation.


2.. Certificate of Recognition Presented to Community Service Officer Cesar Marquez for Exhibiting Extraordinary Lifesaving Actions, and Recognizing Cesar Marquez as an Employee of the Quarter Parks and Recreation Director Alaniz presented the recognition certificate to Cesar Marquez.

Assistant City Manager Domic extended congratulations to Cesar Marquez for being unanimously named Employee of the Quarter. Assistant City Manager Domic expressed gratitude to Marquez for his exceptional contributions and unwavering dedication to his role.

Councilmembers Rebollo, Lainez, Garcia, and Vice Mayor Altamirano all expressed their appreciation to Cesar Marquez for his outstanding courage and for consistently exceeding the expectations of his job responsibilities.

PUBLIC COMMENT Maria Alvarez raised several concerns about the bike lanes on Eastern, expressing that they are ineffective and causing traffic slowdowns. She also noted the absence of a crossing guard at Atlantic and Harbor. Furthermore, she pointed out that two motels are occupying residential parking, suggesting that designated parking spaces should be marked to regulate this issue. Additionally, Alvarez highlighted the overgrown trees on Harbor and Garfield and requested the cleanup of the alley near Atlantic and Harbor. She emphasized the need for a light on Garfield near the apartment complex due to safety concerns in that dark area.

Antonia Lupercio requested that the City Council hire more library staff to extend library hours for the public. Mayor Argumedo responded by informing the audience that the City Council had recently approved several positions for the Library, and if necessary, more positions would be considered during the mid-year budget review.

Mayor Argumedo also mentioned that the City had received a complaint letter from Elizabeth Prada, and copies of the letter are available at the City Clerk's Office for anyone who may need a copy.





CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo The Mayor requested that items #7 and #9 be set aside for discussion.

Regarding Item #7, Acting Public Works Director Nila clarified that the concept was previously approved by the City Council and currently before the City Council for approval is the  Professional Services Agreement pertained to conducting a traffic analysis and formulating recommendations for the final design plan, which would later be presented to the Council for approval.

However, no motion was made for Item #7, resulting in it not progressing further.

For Item #9, Fleet Maintenance Manager Greg Guzman gave a concise overview. In response to Vice Mayor Altamirano's question about the size of the lot, Guzman stated that the lot is large and the substation covers an area of 20,000 square feet. He also mentioned that Edison had removed their equipment and was responsible for addressing soil contamination issues.

Vice Mayor Altamirano moved, seconded by Councilmember Lainez, to adopt a Resolution accepting the Easement Quit Claim Deed at 5926 Sheila Street associated with the Southern California Edison (SCE) Refuse 66-12kV Substation Removal.  The motion was unanimously approved.


5.. Agreement with the Franchise Tax Board for Participation in a Data Exchange Program

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 6A, 6B, and 6C

4.. Approval of Minutes

6.. Professional Services Agreement with Foster and Foster Actuaries and Consultants to Provide a Detailed Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) Statement No. 75 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) Other than Pensions Actuarial Consulting Services

SCHEDULED MATTERS

11.. Appeal to Traffic Commission Denial of Disabled Blue Curb Parking Request at 7158 Watcher Street  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Acting Public Works Director Nila conveyed that they initially presented this matter, and the staff was instructed to gather additional information from the applicant or owner. The applicant, who is the renter, cannot share the driveway with the owner of the other unit that is on the backl. Regrettably, the owner is unwilling to widen the driveway, citing the high associated costs.

Assistant City Manager Domic added that no repairs or vehicle maintenance activities were observed in the parking spaces. The Community Service Officers (CSOs) were tasked with monitoring that area. To date, there have been no reports of any illegal parking or illicit activities in the area.


12.. Appeal of Traffic Commission Denial of Disabled Blue Curb Parking Request at 2305 Connor Avenue  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Acting Public Works Director NIla provided an overview.  Discussion took place.  Should the City Council decide to add another blue curb, it would significantly reduce parking options for other residents, especially since there are already two blue curbs in close proximity.

Councilmember Rebollo suggested implementing parking markings throughout the city to better monitor parking behavior and make spaces more accessible for everyone. Mayor Argumedo raised the concern of addressing those who use street parking for extended periods to sell vehicles, and the discussion continued regarding the possibility of relocating a blue curb closer to the applicant's residence, considering the apparent underutilization of the other blue curb.

Mayor Argumedo motioned to uphold the Traffic Commission's decision. However, the Mayor withdrew the motion after the applicant shared her difficulties in using the other two parking spaces. Councilmember Rebollo recommended moving the blue curb closer to the applicant's home to alleviate the burden of walking a considerable distance.



13.. Slauson Corridor Improvements from I-5 to I-710 Project Concept Plan Greg Garces, a representative from KOA, delivered a detailed presentation outlining proposed changes to the Slauson Corridor. Orlando Silva voiced his strong support for enhancing Slauson Avenue.

Discussions ensued among council members, with a focus on the proposed changes. Councilmember Rebollo her on-site examination of the suggested alterations, particularly underscoring the significance of bike lanes for future sustainability. Councilmember Rebollo highlighted the necessity of presenting complete streets to secure grants and recommended utilizing curbed medians for separating bike lanes.

Councilmember Lainez acknowledged the need for improvements along Slauson, noting that the design is financed by Measure R funds, with implementation reliant on grants that mandate the inclusion of bike lanes for eligibility. 

In response to Councilmember Garcia's inquiry about lane elimination, Mr. Garces clarified that one lane would be removed, reiterating that studies and data analysis suggested maintaining an acceptable level of service post-improvements.

Mayor Argumedo shared insights from a personal visit to Slauson, highlighting the potential impact on the community, particularly with upcoming projects in the Veteran’s Park area. He expressed concerns about the insufficiency of parking and the projected increase in traffic, advocating for traffic improvements without the removal or obstruction of existing lanes.

Acting Director Nila highlighted the financial implications, explaining that if the proposed bike lanes were not implemented, Measure R funds would need to be returned, and future grants would not be secured. Mayor Argumedo stressed the sacrifices being made for future gains but recommended against approving the elimination of lanes.

Mayor Argumedo urged council members to consider the ramifications of lane elimination. Vice Mayor Altamirano aligned with the Mayor’s concerns and recommended against approving the project.

A motion to approve the staff recommendation was made by Councilmember Rebollo and seconded by Councilmember Lainez, but it did not pass.

The subsequent motion to table the item to the next Council meeting was proposed by Mayor Argumedo and seconded by Vice Mayor Altamirano, which was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano and Mayor Argumedo (4)
NAYES: Councilmember Lainez (1).

Orlando Silva reiterated concerns about traffic impact, emphasizing the need to progress towards a more sustainable environment encouraging greater use of public transportation and bike lanes.

ORDINANCES

15.. Adoption and Second Reading by Title Only and Waive Further Reading of an Ordinance Regarding Mobile Food Vendor Regulations This item was continued to the next meeting.  

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo reported her attendance at an Industrial Council event, and also encouraged the community to sign up their kids for sports. She also extended congratulations to the Water Polo Team for their participation in tournaments.

Councilmember Lainez reported that on September 28, he joined the Commerce Business Council event; on the 29th, participated in the ribbon-cutting at Dodger Clubhouse at Citadel; on October 4, worked with Tree People to plant trees along Trigs on California Clean Day. Councilmember Lainez expressed gratitude to the City staff who provided assistance.

Mayor Argumedo reported that he attended the Industrial Council; on September 30, was present at the 36th annual YMCA Gala Roaring event; on October 4, organized and attended a luncheon for the Public Works staff, acknowledging their great work on the outside patio at the Council kitchen. Additionally, participated in "Coffee with Paul Parzik," the executive director of YMCA, who is departing for a new position.

City Council recessed to Closed Session at 7:00 p.m.
